title: Client Services Bulletin: Add-On Test Limits by Service Class (Laboratory Test Orders)
content:
An add-on is a test added to an existing Laboratory Test Orders accession and performed on the specimen already in the laboratory. Each service class sets how long after collection an add-on request is accepted, how many add-on tests one accession may carry, and whether the request must come from the ordering provider.

| Service class | Add-on window (calendar days after collection) | Maximum add-on tests per accession | Requested only by the ordering provider or their office |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routine Clinical Testing | 3 | 4 | Yes |
| Specialty Clinical Testing | 5 | 3 | Yes |
| Esoteric Reference Testing | 7 | 2 | Yes |
| Molecular Infectious Disease Testing | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| Clinical Toxicology Testing | 10 | 3 | Yes |
| Anatomic Pathology & Cytology | 0 | 0 | Yes |
| Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing | 30 | 1 | Yes |

**How the window figure reads.** The window is counted in calendar days with the collection date as day 0, so the figure is the last day, after the collection date, on which an add-on request is still accepted. A window of 0 means the class accepts no add-ons; Anatomic Pathology & Cytology is the only such class, and its maximum is likewise 0.

**Worked reading (hypothetical dates).**

| Class | Collection date | Last day an add-on request is accepted |
|---|---|---|
| Routine Clinical Testing | 10 March | 13 March |
| Esoteric Reference Testing | 10 March | 17 March |
| Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing | 10 March | 9 April |

**Comparing the classes.** The longest window belongs to Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing (30 days), which allows a single add-on per accession; Routine Clinical Testing has a short window (3 days) but allows the most add-ons (4). Every class requires the request to come from the ordering provider or that provider's office.
